# synology_rsync (Resource)

Rsync network-backup service policy. Account credentials and custom configuration remain outside this resource. Destroy leaves DSM settings unchanged.

## Adopt existing settings

Use an initialized project from [Check the NAS connection](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/elephant-evergreen/synology/latest/docs#check-the-nas-connection). Add this import block with your resource address and the ID of the existing DSM object.

```terraform
import {
  to = synology_rsync.main
  id = "rsync"
}
```

1. Add the resource block with the values DSM currently reports. Use the sample configuration as a starting point.
2. Run `terraform plan -out=adopt.tfplan`. For one import, expect `1 to import, 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy`. If the plan proposes changes, match the differing arguments to DSM and save a new plan.
3. Run `terraform apply adopt.tfplan` once the saved plan contains only the import. The next `terraform plan` should report `No changes`.

## Example configuration

```terraform
resource "synology_rsync" "main" {
  enabled          = false
  accounts_enabled = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `accounts_enabled` (Boolean) Enable rsync-specific accounts. This does not create or rotate account credentials.
- `custom_configuration_enabled` (Boolean) Enable the existing custom rsync configuration. This resource does not edit its text.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Enable the rsync network-backup service.
- `ssh_port` (Number) Rsync SSH port, from 1 to 65535.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Singleton identity and import identifier: rsync. Destroy only releases Terraform management; it never resets DSM settings.
